title: 393. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Vector Addition in Plane Geometry
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Add two planar vectors by components.
questions.question: What is \(\langle2,3\rangle+\langle4,-1\rangle\)?
questions.explanation: Add corresponding components: \(\langle2+4,3-1\rangle=\langle6,2\rangle\). The other choice subtracts the vectors.
questions.hint: Combine horizontal components separately from vertical components.

questions.question: What is \(\langle-3,5\rangle+\langle1,-7\rangle\)?
questions.hint: Preserve each component's sign during addition.

questions.learningObjective: Sum consecutive displacement vectors from three points.
questions.question: Let \(A=(1,2)\), \(B=(4,6)\), and \(C=(2,9)\). What is \(\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}\)?
questions.explanation: The vectors are \(\langle3,4\rangle\) and \(\langle-2,3\rangle\). Their sum is \(\langle1,7\rangle=\overrightarrow{AC}\).
questions.hint: Consecutive displacements combine into the displacement from start to finish.

questions.learningObjective: Express and add directed planar movements.
questions.question: Take east as positive horizontal and north as positive vertical. A displacement of \(5\) units east and \(3\) north is followed by \(2\) west and \(4\) south. What is the resultant vector?
questions.explanation: The displacements are \(\langle5,3\rangle\) and \(\langle-2,-4\rangle\). Their sum is \(\langle3,-1\rangle\).
questions.hint: Assign negative signs to westward and southward movements.

questions.learningObjective: Apply scalar multiplication before vector addition.
questions.question: If \(\mathbf{u}=\langle3,-2\rangle\) and \(\mathbf{v}=\langle-1,5\rangle\), what is \(2\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}\)?
questions.explanation: First \(2\mathbf{u}=\langle6,-4\rangle\), then add \(\mathbf{v}\) to obtain \(\langle5,1\rangle\). The factor does not multiply \(\mathbf{v}\).
questions.hint: Apply the scalar only to the vector it directly multiplies.

questions.learningObjective: Recover one addend from a resultant and the other addend.
questions.question: If \(\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}=\langle7,1\rangle\) and \(\mathbf{u}=\langle2,-3\rangle\), what is \(\mathbf{v}\)?

questions.learningObjective: Add adjacent side vectors to locate an opposite vertex.
questions.question: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(A=(1,1)\), \(\overrightarrow{AB}=\langle3,0\rangle\), and \(\overrightarrow{AD}=\langle1,4\rangle\). What is \(C\)?
questions.explanation: The diagonal vector is \(\overrightarrow{AC}=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{AD}=\langle4,4\rangle\). Adding it to \(A\) gives \(C=(5,5)\).
questions.hint: A displacement vector must be added to the starting point to obtain a vertex.

questions.learningObjective: Add three planar vectors with component cancellation.
questions.question: What is \(\langle4,1\rangle+\langle-4,6\rangle+\langle0,-2\rangle\)?
questions.explanation: The horizontal sum is \(4-4+0=0\), and the vertical sum is \(1+6-2=5\).
questions.hint: Check which components cancel before finishing the addition.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a vector parameter from a required resultant direction.
questions.question: The sum \(\langle a,2\rangle+\langle3,-5\rangle\) is a nonzero vertical vector. What is \(a\)?
questions.explanation: The sum is \(\langle a+3,-3\rangle\). It is vertical exactly when \(a+3=0\), so \(a=-3\); its vertical component is nonzero.
questions.hint: A vertical resultant must have zero horizontal component.

questions.learningObjective: Add vectors before calculating the resultant length.
questions.question: What is the magnitude of \(\langle3,4\rangle+\langle-3,4\rangle\)?
questions.explanation: The sum is \(\langle0,8\rangle\), whose magnitude is \(8\). Adding the two separate magnitudes, each \(5\), does not give this resultant.
questions.hint: Compute the resultant components before using the length formula.
